arithmeticInstruction_borrow-complete: Minuends 10–18 and subtrahends 9–1. This complete table has 45 cases requiring regrouping, including subtraction from 10. A dash means outside this range, not an answer of zero.

numbers.title: Numbers and place value
numbers.text: One ten and seven ones represent 17. The digit 1 in the tens place represents 10; 7 in the ones place represents 7. The number of beads is not the quantity represented.

calculation.title: Make ten and calculate
calculation.text: Start with groups of 8 and 6. Split 6 into 2 and 4; combine 8 and 2 to make 10, then add the remaining 4. The diagram shows the groups. Try the interactive ten-frame in the next step, or explain using real counters.

relations.title: Whole and parts
relations.text: Two groups contain 5 and 7 paper counters, making 12 in all. Add to find the whole from its parts. Subtract to find one part from the whole and the other part. The same whole connects two subtraction equations.

shapes.title: Shapes and classification
shapes.text: Observe a cuboid, cube, cylinder and sphere. Each card represents one model, making four models in all. Sort by shape and examine flat and curved surfaces. The drawings do not determine the sizes of real objects.

For diagrams without seams, boundary coordinates use the upper-left origin and shared intervals. Original positions or boundary segments: {description}.
squareMosaicResult: {count} pieces placed, {remaining} remaining; full outline: {shape}. Diagram actions do not replace physical confirmation.
squareMosaicControls: Use position buttons to remove or replace one piece; remove before moving elsewhere. The supply is fixed and each step saves separately. Do not add pieces to complete a pattern.
triangleMosaicNotice: Original mosaics of congruent triangles. The upper-left reference is one piece at the same scale and is not part of the mosaic. Move or turn without cutting, overlap or adding pieces; grid intervals are not centimetres.
triangleMosaicDiagram: Triangle mosaic on a 6-column, 4-row board. The upper-left reference is one piece at the same scale. Coordinates start at the board’s upper left and increase rightward and downward. Original vertices or boundary segments: {description}.
triangleMosaicResult: Full outline: {shape}. Web actions do not replace physical confirmation.
triangleMosaicControls: Select a lettered piece, then move one interval or turn a quarter circle. Other pieces stay fixed. The supply is fixed and each step saves separately.
collageNotice: Original examples made from mixed shapes, with letters identifying pieces at one common scale. Intervals are not centimetres. Count clearly outlined material pieces, not larger outlines formed by combining pieces; interpretations may differ.
collageDiagram: Mixed-shape artwork. Coordinates increase rightward and downward from the board’s upper left, with dimensions in shared units. Letters identify pieces. Original material positions and outlines: {description}.
classificationRecordNotice: Classification record: each symbol represents one item. Symbol shape and arrangement do not change quantity. Read each category label before counting. Categories may use different or identical symbols. A blank group has no recorded items.
surveyNotice: Read the survey question and category labels first. Each mark represents one item. An unrecorded blank is not zero; zero means the category was checked and has no items. Examples and real surveys are separate.
surveyIncomplete: Some categories are unrecorded. Do not total blanks as zero.
surveyTotal: Recorded total: {total} items. Check each against the actual survey population.
surveyLocal: Record category counts without names. Each category allows 0–60, with a total up to 100; parents may assist. Saved in this browser for this course step/task. Filling the web table does not automatically confirm physical surveying.
blockCardsNotice: Original block cards, one block per card, shown separately so no block is hidden. Use the stated criterion: solid features for shape, and written colour labels plus outline colour for colour. Card frames and projected faces are not extra blocks. These illustrations are not centimetre measurements.
natureCardsNotice: Original classification cards: one object per card. Different letters count separately even for the same category. Classify leaves by the shown outline (elongated, fan-shaped or lobed) or written colour; stems, veins and card frames are not extra leaves. Stylized outlines do not identify tree species or describe all plants.
poolSceneNotice: Original pool scene: one person per letter. Sections show location; labels explicitly identify child/adult and red/blue/no ring. Count rings as shown; do not infer swimming ability or safety from a ring. Ask classification questions about the picture; no real pool activity is required.
cupCardsNotice: Original cup cards: one cup per card. Compare straight-sided and tapered bodies while ignoring handles; handle presence and colour are separate criteria. Rims, handles and card frames are not extra cups. These diagrams are not centimetre measurements and do not establish capacity.
childActivitiesNotice: Original child-activity cards: one child per letter, with the shown activity and shirt colour explicitly labelled. Use one criterion; balls, ropes, hoops and card frames are not extra people. Current activity does not establish preference or ability. Holding a hoop does not imply spinning it. This example is not actual class data and does not require physical imitation.
zeroChartNotice: This complete chart starts at 0. Row order stays fixed. Scroll inside the table on narrow screens. The diagram remains read-only when hints are shown.
frameNotice: This frame comes from the 0–99 chart. One number is given. Fill the remaining cells in letter order; a blank is not zero. The diagram stays read-only and does not show missing answers.
frameLayout_square: Square number frame with two rows and two columns
frameLayout_cross: Cross number frame: top, left, center, right and bottom
estimateReference: The dashed box contains 10 verified dots as a reference. Estimate first, then count individually or in groups; area alone does not determine quantity.
estimatePicture: Estimation dot picture with 10 reference dots and additional dots to count
estimateReferenceDot: One dot inside the reference box
estimateDot: One dot outside the reference box
estimateLock: Save initial estimate and start counting
estimateKeep: The saved estimate stays unchanged. Counting does not automatically grade the estimate or confirm physical activities.
counterNotice: One bead on the tens rod represents one ten; one on the ones rod represents one unit. An empty rod contains no beads; the rod positions stay fixed.
counterPicture: Place-value counter with tens and ones rods
counterBead_tens: One bead representing one ten on the tens rod
counterBead_ones: One bead representing one unit on the ones rod

regroupPicture: Bundles of ten and loose sticks
regroupNotice: Each bundle contains ten sticks; each loose stick represents one. The picture shows this step only. Exchanging a bundle preserves the total. Frames and labels are not extra sticks, and the loose-stick count is not necessarily the ones digit.

regroup_subtract_regroup: One bundle opened; {amount} sticks have not yet been removed
regroup_subtract_result: Sticks remaining after removing {amount} loose sticks
stockNotice: Each row represents one item type; units appear beside its name. A, B and C are blanks for remaining stock, not zeros or amounts sold. Only given information is shown. On narrow screens, scroll inside the table to see the remaining column.
stockBlankNotice: Remaining quantity, blank {letter}; unfilled, not zero
crossPool: Available numbers: {values}. Use each number exactly once.
crossNotice: A, B, C, D and E label blanks, not filled numbers. Each line has three positions sharing centre C, which holds one number card. The two line sums must match; they are not required to equal ten.
crossPicture: A top, B left, C centre, D right, E bottom; horizontal and vertical lines
crossLines: Fill A, B, C, D, E. Check vertical A+C+E and horizontal B+C+D separately. More than one placement can work; the picture and hints do not reveal filled answers.
comparisonRowsTitle: Two rows matched one to one
comparisonRowsNotice: Each mark represents one item of the same unit. A dashed connection is a pair, not another item. Rows share a starting point; only original quantities are shown, without the difference.
comparisonRowsPicture: Circles in row A and squares in row B, equally spaced and aligned from the left
comparisonBarsReference: Known A: {count} items of the same unit
comparisonBars_more: B has {count} more items than A
comparisonBars_less: B has {count} fewer items than A
comparisonBarsNotice: The diagram is not drawn to numerical scale. Do not measure lengths to guess quantities. Numbers are given conditions; the dashed segment represents the difference, not another type of item.
comparisonBarsPicture: A is the known reference and B is unknown; the question mark refers to all of B. Only given conditions are shown.
comparisonBarsUnknown: The question mark asks for all of B, not the difference. Read the given conditions before choosing an operation.
houseViewTitle: House box: positions and candidate views
houseViewNotice: The object is opaque and its four vertical faces have fixed features. A–D look toward the centre, perpendicularly at the middle height of each face. This task uses straight-on views, not corner views.
houseViewPlan: Position diagram from above: A at the top, B right, C bottom and D left, all facing the centre
houseViewKnownSide: Given face on the {position} of the diagram: {feature}

houseFace_windows: Two windows, no door or circle
houseFace_circle: One central circle, no door or windows
houseFace_blank: Blank wall, no door, windows or circle
motionTitle: Three position pictures of the same car
motionCondition: P and the viewpoint stay fixed. The same car keeps moving {direction} along a straight road without turning back. A/B/C label pictures, not their time order.
motionFrameDescription: Picture {letter}: car moving {direction}; car centre at diagram coordinate {position}, fixed P at {landmark}. Coordinates describe the drawing for accessibility, not time or measured distance.
motionNotice: Side-view diagrams use the same car size; P stays fixed. Compare car positions relative to P. Picture sizes, letters and drawing coordinates do not label time. P stands beside the road; the car does not collide with it.
occlusionTitle: Opaque box and small cup: positions and candidate views
occlusionConditions: There are always one opaque box and one narrower, shorter cup. The cup is centred on the {side} side of the box. Observers look straight along the arrows, without looking obliquely or down. Neither object moves. When aligned, the box can fully hide the farther cup.
occlusionPlan: Known arrangement: one box and one cup centred on its {side} side. A is above, B right, C below, D left, facing the centre. This plan is not their eye-level photograph.
occlusionPicture_hidden: Only the box outline is visible; no cup outline
occlusionPicture_front: The cup overlaps in front of the box; the upper box remains visible
occlusionPicture_left: Cup on the left of the picture, box on the right
occlusionPicture_right: Box on the left of the picture, cup on the right
occlusionNotice: Candidates are simplified straight-on views under the stated conditions, not transparent views. A fully hidden cup has no dashed or hidden outline. Picture left/right depends on the observer facing direction, not directly on plan left/right. Changes in eye height, distance or angle may change occlusion; verify them physically.

mathStoryTitle: Original math comic: borrowing from a small bookshelf
mathStoryConditions: Read frames 1–4 in order. All events concern shelf {shelf}; there is only this borrowing and return. Returned books came from this borrowing, and each book is counted once.
mathStory_initial: At first: shelf number {shelf} contains {quantity} books.
mathStory_borrow: Next: {quantity} books are borrowed from this shelf.
mathStory_return: Later: {quantity} of those borrowed books are returned to this shelf.

mathStoryDrawingNotice: People, shelf and book icons illustrate the events. Use each frame’s written quantities; the final quantity is not drawn. The shelf number is an identifier, not a book count.

capacityNotice: Only the given team counts are shown; totals and assignments are not supplied. These are original teaching examples, not actual school records. Real activities require school-approved venue and staffing arrangements.

foldCutJoinLabel: Rectangle {width} units wide and 2 units high; {cut}; {stage}. The lower-left corner reflects across the specified line. After cutting, A stays while B moves right; the joining seam remains visible.

foldCutJoinStage_cut: A and B are the two cut pieces. The gap makes them visible. Next, move only B without rotating or cutting again.

sequenceCondition_slide_main: One person slides continuously from the upper left to the lower right without returning or climbing back. The marker 1 identifies the same person; frame letters do not indicate time.
sequenceCondition_slide_review: One person slides continuously from the upper right to the lower left without returning or climbing back. The marker 1 identifies the same person; frame letters do not indicate time.
sequenceCondition_meet_main: Car 1 keeps moving right and car 2 left, each in a separate parallel lane. They approach, meet side by side, then continue without turning back. This is not a collision.
sequenceCondition_meet_review: Car 1 keeps moving left and car 2 right, each in a separate parallel lane. They approach, meet side by side, then continue without turning back. This is not a collision.

sequenceSlideFrame: Frame {letter}: marker 1 is at ({x}, {y}) in a fixed side view. Vertical coordinates increase downward. The slope stays fixed. Coordinates locate the drawing, not time or measured distance.

sequenceTurnFrame: Frame {letter}: the same model from a fixed position, with its nose {direction} and base unchanged. This is an original 3D diagram, not a textbook photograph.
sequenceNotice_slide: The diagram shows positions during continuous sliding, not real distance, speed or elapsed time measured from pixels. Simulate the actual task with a tabletop paper slope or cards and confirm it separately.
sequenceNotice_meet: The two lanes stay fixed. Car numbers identify the same vehicles; positions do not establish real speed or elapsed time. Simulate the actual task with tabletop toys or cards and confirm it separately.

jugViewConditions: An original opaque model with its spout and handle on opposite sides. A–D look straight towards the centre at a fixed eye height. In the two axial views the body hides the far attachment. Both attachments are visible from the sides, with different left–right order.
jugPlanMain: Top-down position plan: A above, B right, C below, D left, looking inward. The spout is on the plan’s left and the handle on its right.
jugPlanReview: Top-down position plan: observers stay in place while the object turns a quarter-turn clockwise. The spout is above and the handle below, looking inward.
jugViewLimit: The plan shows positions from above; candidates are simplified straight-on views under the stated conditions. Picture-left and picture-right depend on the observer’s facing direction. jugPicture_spout-only: Spout facing the observer; the body hides the far handle

jugPicture_spout-left: Spout on picture-left, handle on picture-right; both visible
jugPicture_spout-right: Handle on picture-left, spout on picture-right; both visible
circularTitle: Original circular array: rings and sectors
circularNotice: Four rings are numbered 1–4 from inside out. Ten clockwise sectors are A–J. Blanks show letters only. Moving around a ring differs from moving outward. Scroll inside the diagram on narrow screens.
circularScroll: Scroll horizontally to view the complete circular array
circularDirection: Clockwise sectors: A → B → C → D → E → F → G → H → I → J → A. Returning from J to A stays in the same ring; it does not move outward.
clockCountingDescription: 12 is at the top. Clockwise numbers run from 1 to 12, with five small intervals between adjacent numbers; the full ring returns to its start.
clockCountingLegend: Long marks align with numbers; short marks divide intervals. Count intervals in groups of five, without counting the starting mark twice.
clockCountingNotice: This diagram is for grouped counting only. It has no hands and does not show a time.
partitionedSquareLabel: Original square assembled from separate pieces
partitionedSquareHint: Letters label individual pieces. Interior lines are seams. Compare each piece with the complete outline. These proportions are original, not copied from the textbook.
smallArithmeticInstruction_add: Addition: the row heading is the first addend; the column heading is the second. Each cell holds their sum. Letters identify unanswered cells.
smallArithmeticInstruction_subtract: Subtraction: subtract the row heading from the column heading. Do not reverse them. Letters identify unanswered cells.
bookGroupsInstruction: Original book tokens: {size} books per box. Count groups first, then count all books by group size. Each rectangle is one book token, not a real bookshelf.
lineGridInstruction: Each small interval is 1; numbered long ticks are 10 apart. Letters mark positions. Numbers increase from left to right.
lineGridScroll: On narrow screens, scroll inside the diagram to keep ticks and letters readable.
lineGridLabel: Equally spaced line from {minimum} to {maximum}, unit intervals, with lettered points
pairJoinInstruction: Each example uses two identical pieces, joined along a complete shared edge without overlap or gaps. Compare the separate pieces with the whole outer outline.
pairJoinPiecesLabel: Two identical original paper pieces, shown separately

pairJoinNotice: The internal seam is not an outer edge. These proportions are original examples. Recheck when real pieces or joining edges change; the result does not apply to every triangle or rectangle.
quarterCircleInstruction: Original curved pieces come from equal-size circles cut along two perpendicular center lines. Each piece has an arc and two straight edges. Check the materials, then inspect the whole outline.

quarterCircle_separate: Separated original equal-size curved pieces, each with an arc and two straight edges
quarterCircleNotice: The arc is a curve, not a polygon made of short straight edges. Internal seams are not outer edges. Do not draw missing material as present; mismatched sizes or curvatures may not form a circle.
paradeTitle: Three position pictures of one parade float
paradeCondition: Original side-view model: the float keeps moving {direction} without turning around. Spectator P stays beside the road and the viewing direction stays fixed. A/B/C are picture names.

embeddedInstruction: Original pattern: shading marks its filled area, dotted lines form an evenly spaced grid, and a thick dashed outline marks the whole region to inspect. Material seams are not drawn.

solidInstructionsNotice: Original separated position records: gaps help read relationships and do not imply floating objects. Labels identify the same blocks; this is not an English alphabet lesson.
solidInstructionsGround: Ground arrangement, with the two upper blocks temporarily lifted
solidInstructionsObserver: Stand below the diagram and face the center. Front is nearer, back farther; keep the same viewpoint for left and right.

cubePairGroupLabel: Complete cube shape of candidate group {id}

solidPatternBlank: Position {position} is blank; the diagram does not show its answer
recomposeInstruction: Original block diagrams. Count whole cubes, not faces. Join upright cylinders of equal width with their end faces touching.

tenTablesDiagram: Row {row}, left-to-right symbols: {symbols}. A is filled; B is hollow.

teenLayoutScroll: Scroll horizontally to inspect both ends of the diagram.
teenLayout_rooms: Two rows of rooms with partial number labels and guest positions

teenArithmeticBundle: One bundle of ten; ten sections are not ten bundles

finalPlaneNotice: Count each labelled piece once. Letters, diagram frames and the overall arrangement are not extra pieces.

caterpillarNotice: Choose a number from 1 to 8 for one demonstration turn. This does not score a lesson and restarts on refresh; record actual turn-taking separately.
caterpillarOverflow: {number} beyond the body; take counters away next turn
caterpillarSuccess: Exactly ten: success! Stop this round here.
caterpillarTake: Currently above ten: take away the number drawn next turn.
caterpillarAdd: Currently below ten: add the number drawn next turn.
sixCardNotice: One-player demonstration: 20 paper cards, four of each number from 1 to 5. Draw one random card at a time; there is no added three-card limit. This is unscored and restarts on refresh; real turn-taking and comparison are recorded separately.
sixCardOut: The total exceeds 6: this round is out. Try a new demonstration. This describes the round only.
sixCardFinished: This round has stopped with a total no greater than 6. Compare other players’ valid totals before deciding who wins.
sixCardActive: Draw one more card or choose to stop. Exactly 6 is valid, but another card will exceed 6.
bnuBuildingTitle: Layer record of a building plan
bnuBuildingNotice: Original layer diagram: start with layer 1 on the table and follow the same pieces upward. Left and right refer to this view. Card gaps are reading space, not floating pieces. Do not measure real height or gaps from the diagram or treat it as proof of stability.
bnuBuildingScene_beam: Cylinders support a beam, with one cube above
bnuBuildingScene_gate: Cube bases, cylinders, a beam and two balls above
bnuBuildingScene_tower-flat: Eight-piece plan: the three lower box-shaped pieces lie flat
bnuBuildingScene_tower-upright: The same eight-piece plan: the three lower box-shaped pieces stand upright
bnuBuildingGround: The lowest layer is on the table. Test ball clearance and the stability of the whole building with real objects.
bnuDayClockDescription: Clock: the short thick hand is just past 9; the long thin dashed hand points to 1, past 12.
bnuDayClockNotice: Original observation diagram for printed page 80: just after 9, neither a whole nor a half hour. This task asks only for that distinction, not exact minutes. The face alone does not identify morning or evening.
numberStripTitle: Read the number row from left to right
numberStripNotice: Letters mark blanks, not zero. Follow the rule stated in the question and check left to right. Scroll within the diagram on a narrow screen.
finalColorNotice: These original region cards use a different layout from the textbook picture. Repeated expressions remain separate regions. Cards do not show answers; calculate and select during practice. Colour the original book separately.
triangleRowsTitle: Observe the layers of dots in each figure
triangleRowsDiagram: Original dot figure {position}; count the circles row by row
triangleRowsNotice: Each circle represents one dot. The number of rows differs from the total number of dots. Larger figures keep every dot, including totals above 10. Observing the webpage does not replace drawing the next figures.
finalSolidsTitle_materials: Keep every piece in both material groups
finalFeature_cube: All faces are squares of the same size
finalFeature_cuboid: Rectangular faces with different lengths in adjacent directions
finalFeature_cylinder: Two flat circular ends and a curved side
finalFeature_sphere: A curved surface with no flat face
finalFeature_roof: A solid roof piece with triangular ends, observed separately
finalStability_A: Original plan A: two upright columns support a beam with their flat ends, with a roof above
finalStability_B: Original plan B: a column supports a board, with a ball between two boards and a roof above
finalStability_C: Original plan C: a ball on the left block and two stacked blocks on the right support a beam and roof
finalRobotFigure: Original robot part diagram; observe each part and distinguish painted details from blocks
finalRobotPaint: The eyes and mouth are painted details, not extra blocks. Circular cylinder ends are not extra balls.
finalSolidsNotice_objects: These original overall shape models follow the seven textbook objects but differ in detail. Do not classify by colour or use; inspect the full features of real objects.
finalSolidsNotice_materials: Each card represents one piece. Its orientation and drawn faces do not add pieces. Roof pieces are listed separately, without forcing them into the four basic solid shapes. Match both original textbook structures separately.
finalSolidsNotice_robot: This original equivalent diagram distinguishes separate parts from painted details; it does not bundle the scanned textbook illustration. Check the original book rather than guessing unclear quantities.
finalSolidsNotice_stability: These original supporting diagrams differ from the textbook structures. Pictures do not prove real dimensions, friction or stability. A ball used as a support can roll; physical building is a separate activity.
finalClassificationTitle_legs: Compare the legs of the same animal group
finalClassificationTitle_habitat: Consider the main habitats of another group
finalClassificationTitle_motion: Sort by the stated activity criterion
finalClassificationTitle_objects: Sort all six objects again using a new criterion
finalClassificationObject: Object {label}, {name}: {feature}; {size} in its same-shape pair in this diagram.
finalClassificationObjectsNotice: Original equivalent diagrams do not show measured physical dimensions. Compare size only within each same-shape pair. A multicoloured ball need not belong to a single colour group. Restore all six objects before changing the sorting criterion.
finalClassificationAnimalsNotice: Use the labels and names to identify animals; icons do not establish leg counts, species or activities. The first flying bird has not been identified to species. Use the stated objects, criterion and conditions; animals are not restricted to one activity. Observe the original photographs and explain your own grouping separately.
finalPositionTitle_flower-blank: Use the flower as the reference for the blanks
finalPositionTitle_clocks: Read all four clock faces in A–D order
finalPositionTitle_annex: Nine cards from the textbook appendix
finalFlowerMain: Fixed screen directions: flower in the centre; A above, B left, C below, with the star already on the right. Blank letters do not show the answers.
finalFlowerReview: New fixed screen layout: flower in the centre; A above, B right, C below, with the star already on the left. Follow the new instructions.
finalPositionNotice_flower-blank: This original equivalent diagram preserves the reference and four directions. Record drawing in the actual book separately; a correct screen answer does not confirm it.
finalPositionNotice_flower-filled: A complete teaching example for checking, not evidence that the learner has drawn it. The practice view restores the three blank letters.
finalPositionNotice_items: Use the viewer’s screen directions. Keep two rows and four columns, scrolling inside the diagram on narrow screens. Icons identify objects; row and column positions establish their relationships.
finalPositionNotice_clocks: Original clock drawings reuse whole-hour and half-hour hands. Follow A–D order even when cards wrap. Original matching, physical clock setting and personal time records are separate activities.
finalPositionNotice_annex: Original equivalent drawings of the nine appendix cards, not a new formal unit. Sort by colour, restore all nine, then sort by shape. Draw cards or have an adult help cut them; confirm only activities actually done.
finalFlowerFilledMain: Complete teaching example: square above the flower, triangle left, circle below, star right. This does not confirm the learner has drawn it.
finalFlowerFilledReview: New-condition teaching example: circle above the flower, square right, triangle below, star left. This does not confirm the learner has drawn it.

regionalPresetEnglish: English: no Grade 1 textbook course is available. Keep its current state; a personal set does not establish local English provision or textbook adoption.
regionalPresetReady: Your set for this location, school year and volume is loaded and ready to apply.
regionalPresetUnsaved: This set has changes. Save them before applying.
regionalPresetSaved: Saved in this browser; not applied yet.
regionalPresetRemoved: Removed this saved set. Courses and learning records remain.
regionalPresetRemoveConfirm: Remove the set for this scope? Courses and learning records will remain.
